name: Paper Chromatography
teachingNotes: Paper chromatography separates substances based on continuous partition between stationary cellulose water and ascending mobile phase solvent. Spot positions and Rf values are illustrative for learning.

steps.prompt: Step 1: Draw origin baseline. Choose a marking tool and draw a straight line 1.5 cm above the bottom edge.
steps.hint: Always use an insoluble graphite pencil! Ballpoint pen ink dissolves in solvent and ruins the chromatogram.
steps.completionText: Graphite baseline drawn 1.5 cm from bottom edge. Insoluble carbon line will not bleed.

steps.prompt: Step 2: Spot the sample. Click the Dropper to place a concentrated sample dot onto the pencil baseline.
steps.hint: Keep the sample spot tiny (less than 2–3 mm in diameter) so separated zones remain sharp and clear.
steps.completionText: Sample mixture applied neatly on the origin line and allowed to dry.

steps.prompt: Step 3: Solvent reservoir check. Click the Beaker to adjust developing solvent depth (below baseline!).
steps.hint: The solvent surface MUST stay strictly below the pencil line so the spot does not dissolve into the beaker pool.
steps.completionText: Solvent reservoir filled to 0.8 cm depth, safely below the pencil baseline.

steps.prompt: Step 4: Chamber development. Click the Watch Glass to suspend the paper and cover the chamber.
steps.hint: Covering the beaker saturates internal vapor pressure, preventing non-uniform solvent evaporation.
steps.completionText: Chamber closed with watch glass lid. Mobile phase begins ascending cellulose fibers by capillary action.

steps.prompt: Step 5: Capillary separation. Watch the mobile phase carry and resolve solute components.
steps.hint: Components partition between stationary water film and moving solvent according to relative affinities.
steps.completionText: Chromatographic resolution achieved: yellow dye (low affinity), red dye (medium), blue dye (high affinity).

steps.prompt: Step 6: Mark solvent front & calculate Rf. Click the Paper Strip before the solvent reaches the top.
steps.hint: Immediately pencil-mark the solvent front before the volatile solvent evaporates. Rf = Distance spot / Distance solvent.
steps.completionText: Solvent front marked! Illustrative Rf values: Blue = 0.82, Red = 0.55, Yellow = 0.28. Great job!

pen_ink_selected.message: Mistake! Pen ink contains soluble dyes that dissolve and travel with the solvent, masking your sample spots! Always use a graphite pencil.

solvent_too_high.message: Mistake! The solvent level submerged the baseline! The sample spots washed into the bulk solvent reservoir instead of migrating up the paper.

wrong_apparatus.message: Click the apparatus or tool needed for the current step.
